Nine comments

Evening Prayer Blues

This is an attempt at putting Kevin Burke’s version of Evening Prayer Blues into abc format. I understand the rhythm of the tune but can’t understand the overall structure. The tune plays fine in the Tunebook app. However the musical notation doesn’t look right. Any help would be appreciated. Gregg

↳ Posted by Gregg Harcourt on April 8th, 2015.

I haven’t heard the tune, so can’t comment on that, but the only issues you have are line breaks (most ABC typesetters will break the line of music at the linebreaks, so something like this would look neater:

|G3D GABc|c-d4d3|d4 cBcd|cB G3G Bc|
dg2g2b gd|cBGD CB,G,GBGcB G4-|GD ED:|
G3D GABc|dcBG DCB,G,|BG cG c-d2d-|dcBG DCB,G,|
BdcB G3d-|dcBG DCB,G,|BGcG BGcd-|dcBG DCB,G,|
BdcB G4-|GDED||

Secondly, when writing 2/2 or 4/4 time signatures, there should be a visual break between the two halves of the bar - you should write G3 G- G4 instead of G3 G4- G, for example. So your setting should be written:

|G3D GABc|c-d3- d d3|d4 cBcd|cB G2- GGBc|
dg2g- gbgd|cBGD CB,G,GBGcB G4-|GD ED:|
G3D GABc|dcBG DCB,G,|BG cG c-d2d-|dcBG DCB,G,|
BdcB G3d-|dcBG DCB,G,|BGcG BGcd-|dcBG DCB,G,|
BdcB G4-|GDED||

Note also that abcd will all be beamed together whereas ab cd will be beamed as two seperate groups. Normally you’d want to beam them all together but sometimes it can make a musical point clearer to beam them seperately.

Evening Prayer Blues, X:3

This is my arrangement of the tune that I use for my flute taken originally from a bluegrass mandolin tab. I agree that this piece isn’t Irish music but it’s great stuff all the same, and Bill Monroe was a great American composer and musician. This arrangement will require a flute with keys due to the chromatic notes, but a fiddle shouldn’t have much problem.

↳ Posted by O'Bryan on April 11th, 2015.
